questions.q_en: Constitutional Provisions for Emergency is mentioned in which part of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution_en:
● Constitutional Provisions for Emergency mentioned in part 18 or XVIII of the Constitution of India.

Further Insight:

● Part I: Union and its Territory - Deals with the states, union territories, and the reorganization of territories.

● Part II: Citizenship - Provisions related to citizenship in India.

● Part III: Fundamental Rights - Lists the basic rights guaranteed to individuals.

● Part IV: Directive Principles of State Policy - Guidelines for policymaking to establish social and economic democracy.

● Part IVA: Fundamental Duties - Lists the duties of Indian citizens.

● Part V: The Union - Structure and functioning of the Union Government.

● Part VI: The States - Structure and functioning of State Governments.

● Part VII: Repealed - Initially dealt with Part-B states.

● Part VIII: Union Territories - Administration of Union Territories.

● Part IX: Panchayats - Provisions for rural local governance.

● Part IXA: Municipalities - Provisions for urban local governance.

● Part IXB: Cooperative Societies - Provisions for their functioning and regulation.

● Part X: Scheduled and Tribal Areas - Administration of Scheduled and Tribal Areas.

● Part XI: Relations between the Union and the States - Distribution of powers.

● Part XII: Finance, Property, Contracts, and Suits - Financial relations and management.

● Part XIII: Trade and Commerce - Freedom of trade and commerce across India.

● Part XIV: Services under the Union and the States - Provisions regarding civil services.

● Part XIVA: Tribunals - Provisions for administrative and other tribunals.

● Part XV: Elections - Provisions for conducting free and fair elections.

● Part XVI: Special Provisions - Safeguards for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other weaker sections.

● Part XVII: Official Language - Provisions regarding languages in India.

● Part XVIII: Emergency Provisions - Provisions for handling emergencies in the country.

● Part XIX: Miscellaneous - Provisions on various matters not covered elsewhere.

● Part XX: Amendment of the Constitution - Procedures for constitutional amendments.

● Part XXI: Temporary, Transitional, and Special Provisions - Special provisions for certain states and regions.

● Part XXII: Short Title, Commencement, Authoritative Text - Deals with the title and commencement of the Constitution.

questions.q_en: How many types of emergency are mentioned in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution_en:
• There are 3 types of Emergency mentioned in the constitution of India.

• 3 types are

○ National Emergency

○ State Emergency or President Rule

○ Financial Emergency

Further Insight:

• National Emergency mentioned under Article 352

• State Emergency or Constitutional Emergency or President rule mentioned under Article 356

• Financial Emergency mentioned under Article 360.

questions.q_en: National Emergency is mentioned under Article ___________.
questions.solution_en:
• National Emergency is mentioned under Article 352

Further Insight:

• National Emergency (Article 352)

○ National Emergency can be proclaimed based on:

■ War

■ External aggression

■ Armed rebellion

○ The term "armed rebellion" replaced "internal disturbance" through the 44th Amendment Act.

○ Can be declared even before the actual occurrence of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.

○ Parliamentary Approval and Duration

■ Proclamation must be approved by both Houses within 30 days.

■ If Lok Sabha is dissolved, it must be approved within 30 days of its first reconstitution sitting.

■ Once approved:

• Emergency continues for 6 months.

• Can be extended indefinitely with parliamentary approval every 6 months.

■ Requires special majority in both Houses for approval or extension.

○ Revocation of Proclamation

■ Can be revoked anytime by the President without parliamentary approval.

■ Must be revoked if Lok Sabha passes a resolution disapproving it by simple majority.

questions.q_en: What is the other name of the State emergency or Constitutional Emergency?
questions.solution_en:
• State Emergency is called President rule because when a state emergency is in force all executive power of the state government is assumed by the President.

Further Insight:

• President's Rule

○ Article 355 obligates the Centre to ensure that the governance in every state aligns with the provisions of the Constitution.

○ Article 356 enables the Centre to take over the state government in case of a failure of constitutional machinery, commonly known as President's Rule.

○ Grounds for Imposition

■ Under Article 356: The President can issue a proclamation if satisfied that the state's government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.

■ Under Article 365: If a state fails to comply with or implement directions from the Centre, the President can declare that the state's governance has failed.

○ Parliamentary Approval and Duration

■ The proclamation of President's Rule must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within 2 months.

■ If Lok Sabha is dissolved, the proclamation remains valid for 30 days from its first sitting after reconstitution, provided Rajya Sabha approves it in the interim.

○ When President's Rule is imposed, the President gains the following powers:

■ Assume the functions of the state government and powers of the Governor or other state executive authorities.

■ Authorize Parliament to exercise the powers of the state legislature.

■ Suspend constitutional provisions relating to any state authority or body, if necessary.

questions.q_en: Which article states the provisions of Financial Emergency?
questions.solution_en:
• Article 360 states the provisions of Financial Emergency.

Further Insight:

• Financial Emergency (Article 360)

○ The President is empowered to proclaim a Financial Emergency if he is satisfied that the financial stability or credit of India, or any part of its territory, is threatened.

○ The proclamation must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within two months from its issuance.

○ Once approved, the Financial Emergency continues indefinitely until revoked by the President.

○ Effects of Financial Emergency

■ Extends the executive authority of the Union over financial matters of the states.

■ The President can order the reduction of salaries and allowances of:

• Individuals serving in the state.

• Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts.

• All money bills or financial bills passed by the state legislature must be reserved for the President's consideration.

■ The President can direct reductions in the salaries and allowances of individuals serving the Union government.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following fundamental rights can't be suspended in a National emergency?

a. Article 19

b. Article 20

c. Article 21

d. Article 25

Choose the correct option
questions.solution_en:
• Suspension of Fundamental Right means Person can't move to the court for the violation of Fundamental Rights by the State but after 44th Amendment one can move to court if there is violation of Article 20 and Article 21

Further Insight:

• Suspension of Article 19 Rights:

○ Rights under Article 19 are automatically suspended.

○ Rights are restored after the emergency ends.

○ 44th Amendment: Suspension of Article 19 allowed only in cases of war or external aggression.

• Suspension of Other Fundamental Rights:

○ Article 359 allows the President to suspend the enforcement of specified Fundamental Rights.

○ Does not apply to Articles 20 and 21 as per the 44th Amendment.

○ Requires parliamentary approval.

• Does not apply to Articles 20 and 21 as per the 44th Amendment.

• Requires parliamentary approval.

questions.q_en:
In which of the following types of Emergency Judicial review is allowed?

a. National Emergency

b. President Rule

c. Financial Emergency

Choose the correct option
questions.solution_en:
• All three types of Emergency can be scrutinized by the court under Judicial Review.

Further Insight:

• 38th Amendment Act, 1975: Made the declaration of Emergency immune to judicial review (later repealed by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978).

○ Declared the President's satisfaction in invoking Article 356 as final and beyond judicial review.

• 44th Amendment Act, 1978: Repealed the above provision, allowing judicial review of the President's decision to ensure it is not arbitrary.

• Minerva Mills Case (1980): Supreme Court allowed judicial review on grounds of mala fide or irrelevant facts.

• सभी तीन प्रकार के आपातकाल की न्यायिक समीक्षा के तहत अदालत द्वारा जाँच की जा सकती है।

• 38वाँ संशोधन अधिनियम, 1975: आपातकाल की घोषणा को न्यायिक समीक्षा से मुक्त बना दिया (बाद में 44वें संशोधन अधिनियम, 1978 द्वारा निरस्त)।

questions.q_en: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act 1976 overturned the __________ Amendment Act, which made the declaration of National Emergency final and non-justiciable.
questions.solution_en:
• The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act 1976 overturned the 38th Constitutional Amendment Act 1975, which made the declaration of National Emergency final and non-justiciable.

Further Insight:

• 38th Amendment Act, 1975: Declared the President's satisfaction in invoking Article 356 as final and beyond judicial review.

• 44th Amendment Act, 1978: Repealed the above provision, allowing judicial review of the President's decision to ensure it is not arbitrary.
questions.solution_hi:
• 44वाँ संवैधानिक संशोधन अधिनियम 1976 ने 38वें संवैधानिक संशोधन अधिनियम 1975 को पलट दिया, जिसने राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल की घोषणा को अंतिम व गैर-न्यायोचित बनाया था।

• 38वाँ संशोधन अधिनियम, 1975: राष्ट्रपति की संतुष्टि को घोषित किया।

questions.q_en: Which of the following is the method to remove President rule from the State?
options_en: Revocation of emergency by the Lok Sabha
Revocation of emergency by the Rajya Sabha
questions.solution_en:
• The President can revoke the Proclamation of the President's rule.

Further Insight:

• President's Rule

○ Article 355 obligates the Centre to ensure that the governance in every state aligns with the provisions of the Constitution.

○ Article 356 enables the Centre to take over the state government in case of a failure of constitutional machinery, commonly known as President's Rule.

○ Grounds for Imposition

■ Under Article 356: The President can issue a proclamation if satisfied that the state's government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.

■ Under Article 365: If a state fails to comply with or implement directions from the Centre, the President can declare that the state's governance has failed.

○ Parliamentary Approval and Duration

■ The proclamation of President's Rule must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within 2 months.

■ If Lok Sabha is dissolved, the proclamation remains valid for 30 days from its first sitting after reconstitution, provided Rajya Sabha approves it in the interim.

○ When President's Rule is imposed, the President gains the following powers:

■ Assume the functions of the state government and powers of the Governor or other state executive authorities.

■ Authorize Parliament to exercise the powers of the state legislature.

■ Suspend constitutional provisions relating to any state authority or body, if necessary.
questions.solution_hi:
• राष्ट्रपति राष्ट्रपति शासन की घोषणा को रद्द कर सकते हैं।

• अनुच्छेद 355 केंद्र को यह सुनिश्चित करने हेतु बाध्य करता है कि प्रत्येक राज्य में शासन संविधान के प्रावधानों के अनुरूप हो।
